insight: Benchmark paper abstract: gap-first, then contribution, then scale numbers. Never lead with we built X. All 6 benchmarks studied use this.
Map the full space of what COULD be evaluated, then justify your subset. Pre-empts criticism. HELM does this exhaustively, RouterArena uses principles (DDC, Bloom) as lighter version.

Launch strategies ranked: (1) leaderboard-first + paper later = highest adoption (Arena, MTEB), (2) full-package simultaneous = institutional (HELM), (3) paper-first minimal = dead-simple only (MMLU, HumanEval). TaskBench: paper-first + leaderboard-simultaneous.
Never declare a single winner. Frame headline finding as surprising (counterintuitive beats confirmatory for citations). Use numbered declarative findings (HELM pattern) for quotability.

Use dedicated limitations section for static benchmarks. Reframe scope as design choice, never apologize. Build synthetic experiment to characterize one limitation (HumanEval pattern). Scattered limitations only for platform papers.

RouterArena is closest prior work: 5 orthogonal metrics (accuracy, cost, optimality, robustness, latency), normalized deferral curves, principle-based dataset (DDC + Bloom), no variance but large dataset + robustness as explicit metric.

Community benchmark repo: pip-installable package, data on HuggingFace not in repo, README = identity + scale + install + leaderboard link, contributing guide, automated CI evaluation via PR comments.
Blog leads with why this matters (800 words max), paper provides rigor. Never duplicate. Blog ends with surprising finding + leaderboard link. HELM and Arena both execute this well.

We find that X is the universal sentence template for empirical findings in benchmark papers. All 6 studied papers use it. Direct, unhedged, attributes observation to authors. Never hedge your own numbers.
Benchmark papers use two-tier hedging: assert empirical results (We find that X), hedge causal/predictive claims (may, could, suggests). Never use perhaps or it seems. Never hedge numbers.
Terms defined inline on first use in all 6 papers. Two patterns: appositive (Term, definition clause, predicate) or operational (We define X: procedure). Never standalone Definition blocks.

Em-dashes absent or rare in 5/6 benchmark papers. Commas and parentheticals carry all parenthetical content. Only RouterArena uses em-dashes for definitions. Do not over-use em-dashes in academic benchmark prose.

Benchmark papers shift register by section: abstract=accessible+assertive, intro=motivational+rhetorical with However pivots, methodology=precise+procedural, results=declarative+empirical, limitations=honest+confident, conclusion=elevated+forward-looking.
